THE VENDORING CHOICE IS NOW EVIDENCED, not asserted. Read both implementations: solid-js 1.x mergeProps resolves a key with 'if (v !== undefined) return v', @solidjs/signals 2.x merge with 'if (property in s) return s[property]'. Presence, not definedness — so a caller-supplied prop that happens to be undefined erases a declared default under merge. Both call sites here are defaults-then-props, so plain merge was unsafe at BOTH, as form-e0p.2 predicted. The mechanism is now cited in merge-objects.ts's doc comment. Also verified mergeObjects works against a Solid 2 props proxy: propTraps implements getOwnPropertyDescriptor (returning a getter) and ownKeys, so Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors sees the keys and reactivity survives.
